R103 - discriminating PER-ROW joins for the two families R101 left as position-set matches (review 2026-09-25 R97-R101 F2):
nameplate `rendering/jersey/name_{x}_{y}_{z}_cm.*` and rink logo `rendering/logo/texlib_{x}_{y}_{z}.*`, against `stockteamjerseys` rows.
Candidates tested per row (each a full-tuple lookup of the row's own values in the member name set):
  nameplate : (style, teamartid, variant) | (islightcolor, teamartid, variant) | (isdefault, teamartid, variant) | (style, teamartid, jerseyindex)
              | (style, teamartid, fevariant)
  rink logo : (teamartid, style, variant) | (teamartid, islightcolor, variant) | (teamartid, isdefault, variant) | (teamartid, hastie, variant)
              | (teamartid, style, jerseyindex) | (teamartid, style, fevariant)
Reported per candidate: rows resolved / rows; and on the DISCRIMINATING subset only (rows where that candidate's tuple differs from the
reference candidate's tuple) - resolved / subset size. A candidate that resolves the discriminating subset while the reference does not
(or vice versa) is evidence between them; equal columns (fevariant == variant on every row, R56) cannot be discriminated and are reported
as identical. Also: member multiplicity (same path in several archives / loose), per-member stored SHA-256 (archive members: stored
bytes; loose: file bytes), members without any row under the reference candidate. This is a NAMING association, not runtime selection.
Read-only over the archives, the loose trees and `anchors/`. Usage: python r103_nameplate_rink_discriminating_join.py <out.json>
